formalDefinition: ARCSET = {<G,k> | G is a directed graph that can be rendered acyclic by removal of at most k edges}
problemDefinition: ARCSET, or the Feedback Arc Set satisfiability problem, is an NP-complete problem that can be described like the following. Given a directed graph, does removing a given set of edges render the graph acyclical? That is, does removing the edges break every cycle in the graph?
inputDescription: G, a directed graph, and k, the maximum number of edges allowed to be removed
outputDescription: True or False, whether removing at most k edges can make G acyclic
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
certificateFormat: Format: {(u,v)} subset E | at most K edges, removing them leaves the graph acyclic Example: {(2,3)}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This Solver is a brute force solver, which checks all combinations of k edges until a solution is found or its determined there is no solution

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition:
This Verifier takes in an arcset problem and a list of edges to remove from that problem. It removes those edges and then checks if the problem is still an instance of ARCSET
                                            ie. Does this input graph no longer have cycles after these input edges are removed? Returns true or false
